To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the α subunit of DNA polymerase III has two distinct domains, one for single-stranded DNA and one for double-stranded DNA, that both domains have an equilibrium binding constant of approximately 104 M-1, that the single-stranded binding domain is localized to the OB-fold domain and the double-stranded binding domain includes the HhH2 motif, and that both domains are required for optimal activity of the polymerase.
the E. coli α subunit of DNA polymerase III has a dual affinity for dsDNA and ssRNA, and that the ssDNA binding domain is the C-terminus of the protein.
we have determined the affinity of a bacterial replicative polymerase for both double- stranded and single-stranded nucleic acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure-function relationship of the α subunits of the replicative polymerases.
the interaction between DNA and the replicative DNA helicase and polymerase.
the structure and function of the α subunits of the replicative polymerase of Escherichiae coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the α subunit binds to double-strand DNA and single-strand DNA, and that the double-strand DNA binding is mediated through a tandem HhH2 motif, while single-strand DNA binding occurs through the C-terminal OB-fold.
the OB-fold of α binds to ssDNA and the tandem HhH2 motif to dsDNA, with the two binding modes being mutually exclusive.
the α subunit of polymerase III binds to dsDNA with high affinity and stabilizes the DNA duplex, while it binds to ssDNA with lower affinity and does not facilitate melting of the duplex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α subunit has a distinct double- and single- stranded binding component, and that the HhH2 domain is a novel dsDNA binding motif.
the α subunit binds both dsDNA and ssRNA, but that these binding events are distinct and localized to separate domains of the α subunits.
the C-terminus of α binds ssDNA and the N-terminus binds dsDNA, with a tandem HhH2 motif contributing to dsDNA binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α subunit has a distinct double-stranded DNA binding subdomain, in addition to its well-known single-stranded DNA polymerase activity.
the α subunit of DNA polymerase III has a dual role in DNA replication.
a single polypeptide can bind both double- and ssDNA, and that this binding is distinct.
